constraints: The full authoritative corpus fits the target context with room for the question and response.
The workload is small enough that retrieval complexity needs measured justification.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Full context may consume more tokens than selective retrieval, but it reduces indexing and ranking failure modes while the corpus fits.
details.errorCorrection: Choose RAG for a measured information-shape or scale problem rather than assuming every knowledge base needs vectors.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Tagged full context preserves authority and can reuse a stable prefix; retrieval becomes a later boundary when the corpus no longer fits or selective evidence improves measured performance.
details.scenarioApplication: Load the corpus with document boundaries, put the changing question after it, and monitor context and latency before adding chunking and ranking infrastructure.
details.transfer: Start with the simplest authoritative context design that fits the workload, then introduce retrieval when corpus growth or relevance evidence justifies it.

messages.text: Immediate indexing and reranking add operational complexity without a demonstrated context or relevance problem.
A retrieval layer and coarse topic chunks add indexing and ranking failure modes before the corpus needs selective access; they do not improve the already fitting full-context path.
An extractive summary can omit authoritative detail needed for broad questions, and a citation added only after dispute is too late for the normal answer.

feedback.reason: The corpus fits and is required broadly, so a structured full-context path is simpler and more authoritative than an unneeded retrieval layer. RAG can be introduced when measured size, latency, or query needs require it.

options.text: Build vectors and a reranker immediately so the changing question can select a smaller context, even though the full authoritative corpus currently fits.
Provide the structured full corpus, place the variable question after it, cache the stable prefix where useful, and introduce RAG only when growth or context limits are measured.
Build a vector index with coarse topic chunks and rerank every question to reduce prompt size, even though the full authoritative corpus currently fits with room for the query.
Create a small extractive summary of the corpus for each request and link analysts to full sections only when they dispute an answer.

prompt: A laboratory has a stable authoritative corpus of 90,000 tokens used for broad questions by a small analyst group. It fits the selected context window, and the changing question can follow the source. Which first-release boundary is proportionate?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not optimize only aggregate retrieval recall; short-step precision and long-procedure completeness can move in opposite directions.
details.errorCorrection: A larger context or top-k cannot restore relationships removed during chunking.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Different source structures need segmentation rules that preserve their local meaning; one global size trades away one content class.
details.scenarioApplication: Evaluate intact checklist steps and procedure paths separately, then validate citations and answer completeness on both query sets.
details.transfer: When corpus shape is mixed, segment by semantic structure and measure each meaningful slice.

messages.text: This helps long procedures but bundles many independent checklist steps, lowering retrieval precision for their short queries.
A larger candidate set does not repair a split prerequisite or noisy short-step chunks; it can add irrelevant evidence.
Sentence isolation removes the prerequisite relationships that the task explicitly requires.

feedback.reason: Different source structures need segmentation rules that preserve their local meaning; one global size trades away one content class. Evaluate intact checklist steps and procedure paths separately, then validate citations and answer completeness on both query sets.

options.text: Keep the fixed chunking and increase top-k until both content types appear.
Segment by source structure, preserve prerequisites, and test both query classes.
Embed each sentence independently and let the answer model reconstruct every procedure.
Apply one much larger chunk size to the whole corpus so long procedures retain context.

prompt: A maintenance corpus has 2,400 short, self-contained checklist steps and 70 long procedures with cross-page prerequisites. One fixed chunk size makes the short steps noisy and splits long procedures. Which first change should the team evaluate?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Overlapping text is a heuristic, not a substitute for an explicit dependency when correctness depends on it.
details.errorCorrection: Numeric order alone does not tell the answer path whether a conditional step applies.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Procedural dependencies are semantic boundaries; chunk boundaries should preserve the conditions that determine whether an instruction applies.
details.scenarioApplication: Use dependency-aware chunks or links and test cases where the prerequisite is true and false.
details.transfer: Preserve the rule and its activation condition in the unit the retriever can return.

messages.text: A fixed overlap may still split the condition from the step and does not encode the dependency reliably.
The number gives order, not the semantic condition; the model cannot safely infer an omitted prerequisite.
Duplicating the entire guide creates large noisy chunks and still does not make the condition-to-step relationship explicit.

feedback.reason: Procedural dependencies are semantic boundaries; chunk boundaries should preserve the conditions that determine whether an instruction applies. Use dependency-aware chunks or links and test cases where the prerequisite is true and false.

options.text: Increase overlap uniformly by 50 tokens across all chunks.
Keep each prerequisite with its dependent step, or retrieve an explicit link with it.
Copy the entire guide into each chunk so every step has all context.
Index each step alone and rely on the model to infer the missing condition from numbering.

prompt: A troubleshooting guide uses numbered steps, where step 4 applies only if step 2 returned code E17. Retrieval often returns step 4 without the condition. What indexing representation best preserves the rule?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A document title is useful metadata but cannot stand in for table headers.
details.errorCorrection: Correct row retrieval is insufficient if field-to-value mapping was lost.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Tabular meaning depends on headers and row association, not just the sequence of cell values.
details.scenarioApplication: Index a normalized row with its field labels, contract identifier, and effective revision; evaluate exact-field questions.
details.transfer: When a source is structured, preserve the structure that defines relationships among values.

messages.text: More dimensions cannot recover the labels that were discarded before embedding.
The title provides document topic but not which value belongs to which field.
Neighboring rows may not be retrieved, and inference can assign a value to the wrong contract field.

feedback.reason: Tabular meaning depends on headers and row association, not just the sequence of cell values. Index a normalized row with its field labels, contract identifier, and effective revision; evaluate exact-field questions.

options.text: Increase embedding dimensions so the row values carry more semantic signal.
Ask the model to infer the missing column from neighboring rows at answer time.
Index each table value with its column label and row identity.
Add the table title to every row and leave the columns out.

prompt: A contract repository contains tables whose columns are ‘effective date’, ‘notice period’, and ‘renewal rule’. Search returns the correct row text but omits its column labels. Which repair should be tried first?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A larger candidate list increases review load and can mask revision-mapping defects.
details.errorCorrection: Do not treat a translation match as proof that the corresponding source is current or aligned.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Cross-language similarity and source identity are separate properties; aligned provenance lets the team evaluate both.
details.scenarioApplication: Use paired language queries and measure whether the returned source IDs map to the same effective paragraph revision.
details.transfer: For multilingual corpora, test retrieval and provenance alignment with paired evidence.

messages.text: This may hide translation mismatches and loses a way to verify which source paragraph and revision supported the result.
This can blur paragraph boundaries and still does not ensure the two language passages refer to the same revision.
More results may expose duplicates without fixing revision alignment or measuring retrieval quality.

feedback.reason: Cross-language similarity and source identity are separate properties; aligned provenance lets the team evaluate both. Use paired language queries and measure whether the returned source IDs map to the same effective paragraph revision.

options.text: Merge both languages into one large chunk so either wording appears in every result.
Raise top-k until a reviewer can find the matching language passage.
Translate every query to English and remove the original language from index metadata.
Compare language-specific and aligned retrieval using paired revision-aware queries.

prompt: A bilingual safety manual has Polish and English passages aligned paragraph by paragraph. Users ask in either language, and current translated embeddings retrieve semantically related but sometimes different revision paragraphs. Which next experiment is most diagnostic?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Eventually consistent cleanup does not meet a contract that forbids serving deleted content after acknowledgement.
details.errorCorrection: A successful build can still be stale relative to a later deletion.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Index correctness depends on the source snapshot and deletion generation, not just successful computation.
details.scenarioApplication: Gate activation on a manifest built against the current generation; otherwise rebuild or apply the deletion before serving.
details.transfer: Treat source/index generation agreement as a release invariant for retrieval.

messages.text: That creates a window in which the deleted source can still be retrieved after publication.
The scenario gives no guarantee of replay, and a timestamp alone does not prove the final index includes the deletion.
The index remains a searchable copy, so source-store deletion alone does not satisfy the removal condition.

feedback.reason: Index correctness depends on the source snapshot and deletion generation, not just successful computation. Gate activation on a manifest built against the current generation; otherwise rebuild or apply the deletion before serving.

options.text: Remove the source from the source store but leave the index active until the next scheduled rebuild.
Reject any manifest built before the current deletion generation.
Trust the build-start timestamp and assume later deletion events will be replayed automatically.
Publish because the vector build completed successfully and delete the old vector afterward.

prompt: An index build starts at generation 410. Before it publishes, a source is deleted and the active corpus advances to generation 411. The build succeeds and contains the deleted source. What publication guard is required?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not substitute model priors for evidence stored in the source.
details.errorCorrection: A matching sentence may be semantically incomplete outside its antecedent context.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Local discourse context can carry referents needed to interpret a passage accurately.
details.scenarioApplication: Retrieve linked adjacent context and verify that the cited text identifies the plan before making the claim.
details.transfer: Chunking should preserve references whose meaning crosses sentence boundaries.

messages.text: Query conditioning can improve ranking but cannot supply the missing antecedent needed to interpret the sentence.
The plan identity is document-specific and should come from retrieved source context.
A disclaimer does not correct an unsupported reference or establish which plan the source discusses.

feedback.reason: Local discourse context can carry referents needed to interpret a passage accurately. Retrieve linked adjacent context and verify that the cited text identifies the plan before making the claim.

options.text: Return the sentence with a confidence disclaimer and retain the current citation.
Ask the model to resolve pronouns using its general knowledge of plan names.
Retrieve the antecedent with the sentence and preserve the section path.
Add the question text to the embedding input so ‘this plan’ is more likely to match.

prompt: A support answer cites a single sentence from a policy chunk. The sentence uses ‘it’ and ‘this plan’, while the preceding paragraph defines which plan those terms refer to. The answer is wrong for another plan. What change best addresses the retrieval failure?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not broaden source scope through aliases unless the source owner confirms the terms are equivalent.
details.errorCorrection: Content hash equality does not imply embedding or retrieval behavior equality when indexed metadata changes.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Metadata changes can affect candidate recall even when body text is stable; evaluate the affected query population.
details.scenarioApplication: Use paired queries that distinguish contractors from temporary staff, then verify retrieved scope and citation support.
details.transfer: Treat headings and metadata as part of the retrieval surface and test their changes explicitly.

messages.text: A global score can hide a role-specific retrieval regression caused by the changed heading.
The observed issue is retrieval behavior, and a successful rebuild does not establish that the renamed section remains discoverable.
That may improve recall but can also make the passage appear to govern both populations without a source-backed alias policy.

feedback.reason: Metadata changes can affect candidate recall even when body text is stable; evaluate the affected query population. Use paired queries that distinguish contractors from temporary staff, then verify retrieved scope and citation support.

options.text: Compare only corpus-wide average similarity scores before and after the rename.
Replay role-specific queries against both headings and verify scope and citations.
Add both headings permanently to every chunk in the section.
Rebuild the index and ship because the body text has not changed.

prompt: A policy team changes only a section heading from ‘Contractors’ to ‘Temporary staff’; the body text is unchanged. Retrieval examples suggest the new heading changes which questions find the section. Which evaluation is most useful before rebuilding the full index?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Never stitch passages across revisions without explicit source authority for that composition.
details.errorCorrection: A paragraph-level text match does not override the manifest’s version state.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Retrieval candidates must be resolved against active source version before answering time-sensitive policy questions.
details.scenarioApplication: Read the active revision with the nearby exception table and preserve that revision in the citation.
details.transfer: Use retrieval for discovery, then confirm currentness and local scope in the source.

messages.text: The relevant exception changed, so an old passage cannot establish the current rule.
Combining revisions can create a rule that never existed in either authoritative version.
A warning does not make superseded evidence appropriate for a current-policy answer.

feedback.reason: Retrieval candidates must be resolved against active source version before answering time-sensitive policy questions. Read the active revision with the nearby exception table and preserve that revision in the citation.

options.text: Fetch the active revision and its changed exception table before answering.
Use revision 8 because it is a direct paragraph match and the body appears unchanged.
Cite the revision 8 paragraph and mention that the source may have changed.
Combine revision 8’s paragraph with revision 9’s table to maximize context.

prompt: A customer asks for a current warranty exception. Retrieval returns the correct paragraph from revision 8, while the active source manifest says revision 9 replaced it last week. The two revisions differ only in an adjacent exception table. What should the answer path do?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Avoid silently copying governed facts into a second source of truth.
details.errorCorrection: Finding a value is not enough when another source fragment controls its scope.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Cross-document relationships can determine the applicability of a value and should travel with retrieved evidence.
details.scenarioApplication: Preserve the appendix link and condition, and evaluate both pre-date and post-date cases.
details.transfer: Design retrieval around the relationship needed to interpret evidence, not only its lexical match.

messages.text: The needed condition may still be separated or ranked below the answer path’s cutoff; this does not test whether the relation is preserved.
That duplicates policy text and can become stale unless the source has an explicit derived-copy maintenance contract.
A query prefix cannot prove that the returned value is governed by the procedure’s date condition.

feedback.reason: Cross-document relationships can determine the applicability of a value and should travel with retrieved evidence. Preserve the appendix link and condition, and evaluate both pre-date and post-date cases.

options.text: Copy the limit into the procedure chunk during indexing.
Add the date condition to the query embedding as a synthetic prefix.
Retrieve the appendix value with its applicability condition and source link.
Increase top-k so the procedure might appear somewhere among additional chunks.

prompt: An index has chunks from both a procedure and its appendix. A question asks for a limit whose value appears in the appendix, but the procedure says the appendix applies only to devices sold after a stated date. The retriever returns the value without that condition. Which change tests the real failure?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not average conflicting evidence when one source is explicitly authoritative.
details.errorCorrection: A summary’s provenance does not guarantee completeness for every query.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Generated summaries are retrieval aids and can lose conditions that control a policy decision.
details.scenarioApplication: Fetch and verify the current original passage before forming the approval answer.
details.transfer: Answer from source evidence after retrieval, especially for conditional policy rules.

messages.text: Derived summaries can omit conditions; the returned summary conflicts with the governing passage.
The source resolves the condition; presenting the summary as equally authoritative creates ambiguity.
The current policy is available and should govern rather than model prior knowledge.

feedback.reason: Generated summaries are retrieval aids and can lose conditions that control a policy decision. Fetch and verify the current original passage before forming the approval answer.

options.text: Use the generated summary because it was created from the source and is shorter.
Combine both statements and say either approval path may apply.
Ask the model to infer whether a second approver is usually required.
Retrieve the eligibility definition with the refund exception and retain both citations.

prompt: An HR knowledge index includes policy text plus a generated summary for each chunk. A query retrieves a summary that says ‘managers may approve exceptions’; the original passage says exceptions require a second approver. What should the answer system rely on?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not declare a chunker adequate from one query shape when content has multiple shapes.
details.errorCorrection: Aggregate traffic frequency alone may not represent consequence or interaction coverage.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A chunking design must serve both standalone content and cross-structure queries.
details.scenarioApplication: Build paired tests for standalone warnings and workflow-linked warnings with their applicability conditions.
details.transfer: Test representative query interactions tied to the decision boundary.

messages.text: That leaves the rare but consequential workflow interaction untested.
Similarity on random text does not test whether a user question retrieves the correct linked warning and step.
That can hide noisy warning chunks that harm the common standalone warning task.

feedback.reason: A chunking design must serve both standalone content and cross-structure queries. Build paired tests for standalone warnings and workflow-linked warnings with their applicability conditions.

options.text: Narrow by product and version, then expand to linked procedure evidence as needed.
Use only frequent warning queries because they dominate production traffic.
Test only long workflows and ignore warning retrieval precision.
Use random chunks as queries and measure embedding similarity.

prompt: A medical-device corpus has many short warning statements and a small number of long installation workflows. A query asks whether one warning applies during step 6 of a workflow. Which evaluation set best tests the chunking choice?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Measure both frequent fact lookups and the smaller procedure-query slice; do not optimize one at the expense of the other.
details.errorCorrection: Broad retrieval, whole-manual vectors, and procedure-only indexing each miss a stated need; scope common lookups by product/version and expand only when procedure context is needed.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Hierarchical metadata and staged retrieval reduce a large flat candidate space while preserving detailed evidence for questions that need it.
details.scenarioApplication: Filter on product/version and retrieve section-level passages; expand to linked procedure context for multi-step questions.
details.transfer: Follow query identifiers to the narrowest useful source unit, then retrieve additional context by an explicit need.

messages.text: Scope is resolved only after retrieval, so irrelevant product/version evidence still enters the answer context.
Whole-manual vectors blur section-level evidence and are a poor basis for precise, multi-section procedure retrieval.
That design optimizes the minority procedure queries while dropping direct evidence for the common manual lookups.

feedback.reason: The query usually supplies product and version, while only a minority needs a multi-section procedure. Use those identifiers to narrow retrieval first, then load deeper linked context when needed.

options.text: Search across all manuals with a larger top-k, pass the candidates to the answer model, and have it discard passages for other products or versions.
Create one vector for each complete manual, tag it with product and version, and rely on document ranking to supply both facts and detailed repair steps.
Index repair procedures as the primary units, retrieve the closest procedure for every question, and use its summary for common product/version lookups.
Filter by product and version, retrieve relevant manual sections, and expand to linked procedure passages only when the question needs the repair sequence.

prompt: A corpus has 2 million tokens of product manuals. Most questions identify a product and version; only a minority need a multi-section repair procedure. The current retriever embeds every paragraph in one flat namespace. What design is a useful next test?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not cross tenant boundaries to compensate for index lag; preserve the tenant authorization filter throughout repair.
details.errorCorrection: Global source currency does not establish a tenant's active manifest; cross-tenant retrieval or showing both revisions leaves serving state unresolved.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A multi-tenant retrieval path can have tenant-specific activation state even when its source repository is current.
details.scenarioApplication: Compare affected requests with their tenant manifest and served generation, then activate the approved rule in the stale tenant scope.
details.transfer: Trace the actual request-scoped index identity when diagnosing version skew.

messages.text: Fetching across tenants before authorization can expose records and still does not establish the tenant's active serving generation.
A current source and global rebuild do not prove tenant-specific activation or served-index state.
Showing both versions leaves the tenant's active policy unresolved and permits the obsolete rule to remain in service.

feedback.reason: The source is globally current, but the tenant manifests differ. Diagnosis therefore needs the request’s tenant-scoped manifest and served generation, not another global rebuild.

options.text: Retrieve the globally newest rule for all tenants, then apply application filtering after retrieval so the affected tenant can see the approved revision.
Rebuild the global index from the current source revision and assume each tenant manifest will begin serving that generation automatically.
Increase top-k for stale tenants so the old and new rules both appear, then instruct the answer model to prefer the newer revision.
For affected requests, inspect that tenant's active manifest and served index generation, then repair its activation against the approved rule revision.

prompt: A document owner approves a new retention rule, but the vector index still serves the previous rule for a subset of tenants. Logs show the source revision is current globally, while tenant manifests differ. What should the diagnosis inspect?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Keep per-slice outcomes visible; the pilot evidence is bounded to this held-out set and does not guarantee future performance.
details.errorCorrection: Each declared slice must clear its support floor; aggregate scores and untested top-k changes do not qualify a design that misses one floor.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A chunking choice should be judged on evidence support for the query types it serves, plus operational constraints such as rebuild time.
details.scenarioApplication: Structure-aware chunking supports 37/40 warning cases and 74/80 simple lookups, meeting the stated 90% floors; its 24-minute rebuild remains below the 30-minute cap.
details.transfer: When retrieval designs trade query-slice quality against operational cost, apply declared floors to each slice before rollout.

messages.text: The fixed design misses the explicit 90% warning-slice floor, which the faster rebuild cannot offset.
There is no evidence the wider retrieval restores warning support while preserving the simple-query floor.
An aggregate hides whether an individual required slice falls below its floor on later cohorts.

feedback.reason: The held-out comparison shows fixed chunks miss the warning floor, while structure-aware chunks meet both slice floors and the 30-minute rebuild cap. Pilot the qualifying design and continue watching each slice.

options.text: Choose fixed chunks for their 20-minute rebuild and stronger simple-lookup score, then accept the warning slice's lower support as the pilot trade-off.
Keep fixed chunks and increase top-k until warning support improves, then rely on the old held-out results to represent the larger candidate set.
Pilot structure-aware chunks: warning support is 37/40 and simple lookup support is 74/80, both above 90%, with a 24-minute rebuild under the cap.
Choose structure-aware chunks from the combined 120-query score, then stop tracking query slices because the aggregate already clears the average floor.

prompt: A held-out retrieval test covers 40 warning-applicability questions and 80 simple lookups. Fixed chunks support the cited answer in 33/40 warning cases and 75/80 simple cases; structure-aware chunks support 37/40 and 74/80. Their rebuild times are 20 and 24 minutes, respectively, against a 30-minute cap. Each query slice has a 90% support floor. Which design qualifies for the next pilot?

constraints: A numeric answer needs the table labels and units in its evidence chunk.
The retrieval location is correct; the source-to-chunk transformation is the suspected fault.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Richer chunks increase index size and may reduce granularity, so evaluate them on numeric recall, citation support, and retrieval cost.
details.errorCorrection: Repair the evidence representation when the source-to-chunk boundary loses semantics; do not mask it with broader retrieval or inference.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Contextualized structure gives retrieval and generation the relationships needed to interpret a numeric row; reindexing and source comparison test whether the repair restores accuracy.
details.scenarioApplication: Include table and section identifiers in each chunk, run torque holdouts with units, and reject answers whose evidence span does not support the numeric value.
details.transfer: When RAG finds the right location but the answer is wrong, inspect chunk structure and contextual labels before changing embeddings or model behavior.

messages.text: More vectors and top-K do not restore the missing heading or unit and can increase distractors while encouraging an inferred value.
A full manual raises context cost and hides the evidence boundary; it is not a targeted repair for a lost table label.
Plausibility is not source support, and accepting inferred units can propagate a silent numeric error.

feedback.reason: The correct section cannot compensate for lost table semantics. Restoring heading, labels, units, and context in the chunk addresses the observed transformation defect before changing ranking.

options.text: Rebuild the chunk with its table heading, column labels, units, nearby procedure context, and section ID, then reindex and evaluate numeric answers against the source.
Increase embedding size and top-K, leave the isolated table row unchanged, and let generation select a plausible unit from nearby retrieved engineering passages.
Place the full manual in every request so Claude can infer the missing heading and unit from surrounding pages instead of changing the index.
Accept a numeric unit when it falls within a familiar engineering range and send only unusually large deviations to a reviewer.

prompt: After an equipment-manual migration, retrieval finds the correct section, but answers misstate a torque value because a table row was indexed without its column heading and unit. What should be repaired first?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Keep contextual text for candidate discovery only when its provenance and version are retained; evaluate annotation errors separately from source retrieval.
details.errorCorrection: A query-matching descriptor does not override the source section’s explicit population boundary.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Generated context can help rank a chunk, but it is derived retrieval metadata rather than an authoritative policy source; scope may depend on adjacent headings and revision state.
details.scenarioApplication: Fetch the active corporate-chargeback passage with its heading, test whether it entails the EU refund claim, and withhold the claim while correcting the mismatched generated context.
details.transfer: Separate retrieval aids from evidence, especially when generated metadata conflicts with source scope.

messages.text: Similarity to the query cannot make generated metadata authoritative when the source heading contradicts its scope.
The heading supplies the population boundary; removing it would erase evidence needed to interpret the passage.
The source states a narrower scope, so presenting both as equally supported shifts an index error to the user.

feedback.reason: The generated retrieval context conflicts with the original section and cannot establish policy scope. Verify the current source passage and surrounding heading before answering, then repair the index annotation that misdirected retrieval.

options.text: Treat the contextual sentence as the governing policy because the retrieval model selected it for the query.
Fetch the active source and heading; answer only if supported, then inspect conflicting generated context.
Cite the retrieved chunk body alone and discard its heading because headings were added only to help retrieval.
Return both interpretations and let the user choose which customer class applies.

prompt: A policy index prepends a generated contextual sentence to each source chunk before embedding. For a refund query, the retrieved sentence says “this rule applies to EU consumer refunds,” but the source chunk is from a global corporate-chargeback section and the adjacent heading limits it to corporate accounts. An engineer proposes citing the generated sentence because it matched the query. What should the answer path do?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the system cannot verify index completion, return a pending deletion state and block claims that removal is complete.
details.errorCorrection: A delay or queued rebuild does not prove that all active derived artifacts exclude R2; ranking lower still leaves deleted text retrievable.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Source deletion and derived-index deletion have separate completion states; versioned builds or tombstones prevent an older asynchronous job from restoring stale chunks.
details.scenarioApplication: Bind publication to the deletion generation, reject any build older than that generation, and check the served index before returning success.
details.transfer: Treat derived retrieval artifacts as part of the source lifecycle and verify their served state.

messages.text: Elapsed time does not establish that a pre-deletion build has finished or that the served index excludes R2.
Queue acceptance is not index publication or retrieval verification, and a stale build can publish afterward.
A lower score changes ranking, not whether deleted text remains available to retrieval.

feedback.reason: A rebuild from a pre-deletion snapshot can reintroduce removed content. The lifecycle must prevent stale publication and verify the active retrieval state before confirming deletion.

options.text: Delete the source row, then wait a fixed hour before telling the tenant the policy is gone.
Attach a deletion generation or tombstone to index publication, reject stale builds, and verify no active index can retrieve R2 before acknowledging removal.
Start a new full rebuild after every deletion and acknowledge immediately when the job is queued.
Lower R2’s retrieval score so current policy text is more likely to rank first.

prompt: A tenant deletes policy revision R2. The source store confirms deletion, but an index rebuild that started before the deletion can finish afterward and publish vectors containing R2. The API must not acknowledge removal while R2 remains retrievable. Which lifecycle control is strongest?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: After the immediate path is repaired, investigate why the contextual sentence conflicts with its source.
details.errorCorrection: More results or prompt confidence cannot replace the missing source evidence.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Contextual retrieval can improve matching but does not turn generated context into authoritative policy text.
details.scenarioApplication: The heading and adjacent paragraph are necessary to interpret the retrieved clause’s scope.
details.transfer: Separate retrieval hints from answer-time evidence.

messages.text: Ranking and provenance do not make a generated sentence authoritative when the cited source excludes the stated population.
The source heading already excludes commercial purchases; ranking two scopes together does not resolve that conflict.
A second model’s impression is not a source check and cannot override the passage’s explicit scope.

feedback.reason: The trace shows that generated retrieval context contradicted the governing source scope. The answer path must ground the claim in the active source passage and its boundary.

options.text: Lower the generated sentence’s rank and require the source revision in its metadata, while allowing the sentence itself to support the answer when it remains top-ranked.
Retrieve both consumer and commercial passages, then select the interpretation supported by the stronger semantic match and show both citations.
Keep the retrieved sentence but require a second model pass to check whether its scope sounds consistent with the question.
Fetch the active source passage with its heading and scope, and treat generated context as retrieval metadata rather than answer evidence.

prompt: A retrieved contextual sentence says a warranty exception applies to commercial equipment. The cited source chunk is from a consumer section; its heading and adjacent paragraph exclude commercial purchases. The answer used the contextual sentence as policy. Which trace-led repair is smallest?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the index cannot prove removal, report the deletion as pending.
details.errorCorrection: Queue acceptance is not successful publication or deletion completion, and lower ranking does not remove data.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Source storage and derived indexes have independent lifecycle states.
details.scenarioApplication: A build-generation fence and served-index verification show whether stale chunks remain available.
details.transfer: Compare deployment artifacts at the layer that serves retrieval.

messages.text: A source receipt and manifest revision still do not establish whether an old chunk remains in the active served index.
Build completion may still publish work based on a pre-deletion snapshot; the active inventory needs a deletion-aware generation check.
A low-ranked deleted chunk remains retrievable and violates the removal condition even below a ranking threshold.

feedback.reason: The manifests show that a pre-deletion build can publish stale chunks despite the source deletion and queue acceptance. The served index must be checked against the deletion generation.

options.text: Use the deletion receipt to close the source record, then check the index manifest’s source revision before treating the rebuild as current.
The active served-index inventory and a retrieval check for R2, tied to a build generation newer than the deletion.
Wait for the accepted rebuild to finish, then compare its manifest with the source revision before retiring the prior index.
Query the active index for known R2 phrases and retire it only if those phrases still rank within the configured retrieval threshold.

prompt: Two index manifests are compared after a policy refresh. Manifest B has the new source revision, but its build began before the deletion event and contains an old chunk ID; its deployment log says “job accepted.” Which artifact should decide whether R2 is still retrievable?

constraints: Boundary-case answers need adjacent exception context.
The index should retain retrieval granularity rather than making every chunk a full manual.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Overlap increases index and prompt cost and can introduce duplicate passages, so use the smallest measured expansion that restores exception recall.
details.errorCorrection: Repair the chunk boundary and context expansion before relying on model inference or unbounded candidate counts.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Section-aware chunking can include the next section or parent context when a cross-reference is detected; evaluation checks whether the exception and citation arrive together.
details.scenarioApplication: Build boundary-case queries, compare fixed and overlap variants, and retain section IDs and neighboring references in the evidence returned to Claude.
details.transfer: For manuals and policies with cross-references, test structure-aware chunks and controlled neighboring context against boundary-case evidence.

messages.text: General knowledge cannot safely supply a missing safety exception and hides the evidence gap.
Whole-manual chunks destroy retrieval granularity and inflate context for ordinary questions.
More candidates may add the next section but does not guarantee adjacency or prevent irrelevant clauses from crowding the answer.

feedback.reason: The failure is a chunk boundary that separates an exception from its governing rule. Controlled overlap or parent expansion restores adjacent scope while preserving meaningful retrieval units and makes the trade-off measurable.

options.text: Keep fixed windows and ask Claude to infer an omitted exception from general safety knowledge when a boundary case is detected.
Make each chunk the complete manual so every cross-reference is present, accepting a large context and losing section-level retrieval precision.
Use section-aware chunks with controlled overlap or parent-context expansion, then compare boundary recall and citation completeness with fixed chunks while tracking index and prompt cost.
Increase top-K until both sections appear, without changing boundaries or testing whether the extra sections introduce unrelated rules.

prompt: A safety manual contains cross-references where an exception starts in one section and its scope continues into the next. Fixed 300-token chunks retrieve the rule but omit the exception on boundary cases. Which chunking change should be tested?

constraints: Deleted revision content must not answer current queries.
Retrieval and citation tests must enforce tenant and active-revision state.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Deletion propagation and tombstone checks add operational complexity and may reduce recall, but they protect retention obligations and citation correctness.
details.errorCorrection: Enforce content lifecycle and authority before generation rather than relying on ranking, recency, or prompt admonitions.
details.mechanismOrProperty: The index lifecycle marks vectors unavailable and the retriever applies tenant and revision filters before evidence is returned; the model is not asked to enforce deletion from mixed chunks.
details.scenarioApplication: Process the R2 deletion event, verify no active query retrieves it, index R3 with its version, and test citations against current and historical modes separately.
details.transfer: For mutable corpora, treat deletion and version filters as retrieval invariants and test them at ingestion, index, query, and citation boundaries.

messages.text: Claude cannot reliably enforce deletion or revision policy when stale and current chunks are both available.
A score preference does not remove deleted content and can still return R2 when the query matches it better.
A prompt note is not an index authorization or retention control and leaves the deleted clause searchable.

feedback.reason: Retention and revision state are index and retrieval responsibilities. Tombstoning or removing R2 and filtering active revisions prevents stale evidence from reaching generation; tests prove the deletion boundary.

options.text: Mark R2 unavailable, remove or tombstone its vectors, filter retrieval to the tenant's active revisions, and run deletion and citation tests before exposing R3.
Leave R2 vectors searchable for recall and instruct Claude to prefer R3 when both revisions appear, treating deletion as a generation preference.
Append R3 vectors and rely on its higher embedding score to make deleted R2 unlikely to be returned by current queries.
Keep R2 in the same tenant index and add a prompt note that historical clauses must not be quoted in current answers.

prompt: A tenant uploads revision R3 and deletes R2 under a retention policy, but R2 embeddings remain searchable and answers cite the deleted clause. Which index lifecycle change is required?

constraints: The corpus is four million tokens and exceeds the selected model window; each query targets one section.
Documents have stable revision and section metadata, and source citations must identify them.
A 500-question benchmark can measure section-aware chunks, reranking, citation recall, and latency.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the active corpus later fits within the model window and broad questions dominate, re-evaluate full context with a stable prefix.
details.errorCorrection: The corpus cannot fit and broad context would exceed both model and cost budgets; it cannot prevent omissions by being rejected before inference.
details.mechanismOrProperty: RAG is useful for retrieving relevant chunks, but it is not always needed when a knowledge base fits in context; prompt caching can help repeated full context. The scenario's mechanism is governed by this decisive constraint: The corpus no longer fits the context window and the query is targeted, so full-context prompting must reverse to an evaluated RAG pipeline.
details.scenarioApplication: Index active revisions into section-aware chunks, retrieve and rerank a bounded candidate set, include source IDs in context, and switch only after citation recall and latency meet the service floor.
details.transfer: Use targeted retrieval when the corpus cannot fit and questions address sections; preserve revision and section identity and measure citation recall alongside latency.

messages.text: The corpus cannot fit and broad context would exceed both model and cost budgets; rejecting the request cannot prevent omissions.
Unfiltered chunks can surface retired sections and cannot satisfy the required active-revision citations or benchmarked evidence boundary.
A first-match shortcut does not establish recall, answer quality, or tail latency for section-specific questions before a production switch.

feedback.reason: The size and query evidence remove the full-context option while leaving a measurable retrieval design to evaluate.

options.text: Keep the full corpus in every request because broad context prevents retrieval misses.
Use active-revision section-aware RAG with bounded reranking and source IDs; switch only after recall and latency meet the floor.
Chunk the corpus once and retrieve by similarity without filtering active revisions or attaching source IDs.
Use a short keyword match and switch immediately, deferring citation and latency evaluation until after rollout.

prompt:
A laboratory corpus has grown to four million tokens, while analysts ask one section-specific question per request. A full-context request exceeds the selected model window, and source citations must identify the active revision and section.

Which retrieval design should replace the infeasible full-context request?

constraints: The inventory API is authoritative for hourly quantity and tenant scope.
Manual retrieval can filter active revision sections, but historical clauses remain during rollout.
The answer must keep source identity visible and stop when the two sources disagree on a restriction.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the inventory API is unavailable, expose quantity as unavailable and provide the manual explanation separately; do not infer current availability from prose.
details.errorCorrection: Semantic similarity cannot guarantee current quantity or tenant scope, and a historical manual clause can outrank the hourly structured record.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Retrieval should match the query and source shape; a structured metric lookup is better served by the metrics source than by semantic narrative search. The scenario's mechanism is governed by this decisive constraint: The pipeline must route each information need to its source shape and keep structured freshness and manual revision filters separate before combining the answer.
details.scenarioApplication: Query the authorized inventory API for the exact SKU and current quantity, retrieve only active manual sections for the explanation, label each evidence source, and abstain or escalate if the two sources disagree on the restriction.
details.transfer: Assign each fact to its authoritative source and freshness boundary; combine structured current facts with versioned explanations and escalate conflicts.

messages.text: Semantic similarity cannot guarantee current quantity or tenant scope, and a historical manual clause can outrank the hourly structured record.
Manual prose cannot establish hourly inventory or tenant scope and may contain historical clauses; the structured API remains authoritative for quantity.
Choosing prose without active-revision evidence hides a source disagreement; the assistant must label sources and abstain or escalate when restriction evidence conflicts.

feedback.reason: The integrated answer preserves source authority and freshness instead of asking one semantic index to answer incompatible facts.

options.text: Run one semantic search over manual and inventory text and let the highest-scoring paragraph provide both facts.
Use the manual corpus as the sole source for availability and restriction because it contains more explanatory context.
Query authoritative inventory for quantity, retrieve active manual evidence for explanation, label sources, and escalate conflicts.
Return the inventory quantity and choose the most recent-looking manual restriction without exposing a conflict state.

prompt:
A parts assistant must answer two linked facts: the exact current availability of SKU AX-4407 and the manual explanation for why the item is restricted. The structured inventory updates hourly; the manual corpus updates weekly and contains similar historical clauses.

How should the assistant combine the current inventory fact with the manual explanation?

constraints: Chunks must preserve section and table meaning.
Document and revision identity must remain coherent while the replacement index is built and switched.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Smaller structured chunks and parallel index builds require more metadata and storage, but they avoid incoherent citations and support rollback.
details.errorCorrection: Treat chunk boundaries and index lifecycle as evidence integrity controls, not just vector tuning settings.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Structure-aware chunks retain local headings, units, and table context; a versioned index lifecycle lets evaluation occur before the new corpus becomes authoritative.
details.scenarioApplication: Tag every chunk with document, revision, section, and table identity, evaluate retrieval and citations on the new build, then switch the active revision as one operation.
details.transfer: For versioned RAG corpora, preserve semantic units and revision identity, evaluate a replacement index separately, and switch authority atomically.

messages.text: Equal windows can split headings and tables, and in-place updates allow old and new revisions to rank together without a coherent switch.
Appending without revision filters leaves incompatible evidence available and asks generation to enforce a lifecycle policy it cannot guarantee.
Whole-document vectors preserve tables but lose section-level retrieval precision and make a large procedure harder to address.

feedback.reason: Section and table boundaries preserve meaning, while immutable revision identifiers and an atomic switch prevent mixed-version evidence during rollout.

options.text: Split procedures into equal windows, update vectors in place, and allow a newer matching chunk to outrank an older one during the rebuild.
Append the replacement chunks to the active index without revision filters and ask generation to reconcile any clauses that cite different versions.
Chunk by meaningful sections and intact tables with immutable document, revision, and section IDs; build and evaluate separately, switch atomically, then retire the old revision.
Index each entire procedure as one vector so tables remain together, accepting poor section precision and relying on document-level citations.

prompt: An operations team rebuilds an index for 40,000 equipment procedures containing headings and safety tables. During rollout, citations must never combine clauses from two revisions. Which indexing design should be selected?

constraints: Similar clauses need local document and location context.
Candidate count and reranking must be evaluated against relevance, latency, and cost.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Reranking and context expansion add compute and tokens, so their value must be balanced with candidate quality and cost.
details.errorCorrection: Improve candidate evidence and ranking separately; do not ask generation to recover document location or choose among an unbounded corpus.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Contextualized chunks carry document and location clues; a reranker scores the initial candidates and the evaluation set links top-K to answer relevance and resource use.
details.scenarioApplication: Add section and jurisdiction context, rerank lexical/semantic candidates, and select a top-K that meets citation and latency floors on regulatory queries.
details.transfer: For similar legal or policy passages, preserve local provenance in chunks and validate reranking and top-K against the actual answer task.

messages.text: The corpus exceeds useful context and leaves evidence selection and source location implicit.
A document-level vector loses the local distinctions that determine the controlling clause and forces generation to search inside a broad unit.
Word frequency misses semantic paraphrases and cannot reliably resolve similar clauses or their local scope.
Without local document and location context, similar clauses remain difficult to distinguish after retrieval.
Without measured reranking and top-K, the pipeline cannot improve precision while controlling latency and cost.

feedback.reason: Local context disambiguates similar clauses, and reranking can improve precision after an initial recall stage when top-K is measured. Both decisions address the observed broad relevance without overflowing context.

options.text: Send the entire corpus to Claude so every similar clause remains available for the answer.
Use one vector for each complete document and rely on the model to locate the controlling clause in generation.
Rely only on frequent-word filtering so lexical overlap determines the final candidate set.
Prepend concise document and location context to candidate chunks so local meaning survives retrieval.
Rerank a measured initial candidate set and tune top-K against relevance, latency, and cost on representative queries.

prompt: A regulatory corpus contains millions of tokens and many similar clauses. Initial retrieval returns broadly related passages, but the answer depends on local context and precise relevance. Which TWO pipeline choices improve evidence quality? Select TWO.
